bindings.label: A 5-day-old male neonate presented with widespread jaundice

The neonate was a 5-day-old male born at term via vaginal delivery, weighing approximately 2100 g; mother had history of six pregnancies and six live births and was generally healthy except for mild photosensitivity; no history of clay-colored stools, fever, or drug administration

On admission, physical examination showed pale conjunctiva, yellowing of the sclera, generalized jaundice, a few red lesions around the eyes, and mild enlargement of the spleen; pulse was irregular with heart rate about 75 beats per minute; electrocardiogram indicated third-degree atrioventricular block; echocardiography revealed patent foramen ovale without other abnormalities

Blood tests showed hemoglobin 9 g/dL and platelet count 80,000/mm3; blood smear indicated erythrocyte hypochromia, anisocytosis, and poikilocytosis; reticulocyte index, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate were within normal ranges; liver function tests were elevated: AST 760 U/L, ALT 187 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 2045 U/L, total bilirubin 12.4 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 6.2 mg/dL; prothrombin time and partial thromboplastin time were normal; TORCH titers, viral hepatitis markers, thyroid function tests, blood and urine cultures for mother and neonate, and tests for galactosemia, tyrosinemia, and phenylketonuria were negative

Abdominal ultrasound showed a normal-sized liver and gall bladder, no bile duct dilation, and no biliary sludge; spleen was mildly enlarged with normal echo pattern; hepatobiliary scintigraphy indicated decreased hepatic uptake with no passage through the intrahepatic bile ducts; initially skin lesions were a few non-scarring red annular plaques around the eyes, and over the next few days they spread to the nasal bridge and upper cheeks, developing sharp and slightly hyperkeratotic borders
Autoimmune serology shows ANA 1:640 and anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB >4 index
